# Brigid

*Herb Gatherer*

|  |  |

## Personality

Shy, gentle and observant; she notices everything and says very little.

## Lore

Brigid is seventeen and the herb gatherer of the Forest Shore, the apprentice of Elspeth the healer. Twice a day, whenever the tide goes out, she is down on the rocks with a flat basket and a short knife, picking the sea-herbs that Elspeth turns into salves and tonics. She is shy, gentle and observant. She notices everything and says very little, and people who talk to her often walk away realising that they have told her a great deal and learned almost nothing about her.

### The girl on the rocks

Brigid does not remember her parents. When she was two, the log raft they were working broke up rounding the point on a bad tide, and neither came ashore. She was raised by her grandmother, Oonagh, who gathered dulse and sea-herbs on the Forest Shore rocks and sold them to the healer and the smokehouses. Oonagh took the little girl out on the rocks from the time she could walk on weed without falling, and taught her the beds one by one: which grew on the sunny side of which rock, which wanted the full tide over them, which could only be cut every third spring.

Oonagh died when Brigid was eleven. Elspeth, who had been buying Oonagh's herbs for thirty years, came to the funeral, looked at the thin, silent girl holding a basket she would not put down, and took her home. Brigid has slept in the loft of the low stone house ever since, among the bunches of drying herbs that hang from every beam, and has been Elspeth's apprentice for six years.

### The craft

Elspeth says there is no magic in the sea-herb craft, only knowing which herb, which tide and which hour, and that the knowing is the magic. Brigid has the knowing already, for the gathering at least. She can tell a bed's health from the colour of its edges at twenty paces, and she knows the hour a herb is strongest by the smell of it on her fingers. The brewing she is still learning, slowly, because Elspeth teaches by doing and Brigid learns by watching, and neither of them says much while they work.

She has seen what the brewing is for. The hunters bring their wounded to Elspeth's door several times a week now, and Brigid holds the bowls and the lamps. She has watched Elspeth stitch Torva more than once, and she has seen Osric, Elspeth's son, sit silent by the fire on his bad nights. Brigid never asks him anything. She thinks that is perhaps why he does not mind her being there.

### The withering beds

Last autumn the oldest beds on the low rocks at the forest end of the shore began to fail. The leaves came up pale, then went soft and dark at the root, and the beds shrank from the bottom edge upward. By this spring five of the eleven beds she has picked all her life were withering, and two of them were nearly gone. She has not found a cause. She has wondered whether she cut them too hard, whether some sickness is in them, whether something grazes them at night. She has also noticed, without knowing what to make of it, that the wrack line on those rocks sits a little higher than it used to.

She has not told Elspeth. Elspeth's great fear is running out of herbs while the wounds keep coming, and Brigid cannot bring herself to be the one who tells her it has begun. Instead she has been walking further along the wild coast at low tide to fill her basket from beds she barely knows, and still coming home with it a little lighter. Elspeth has noticed the lighter baskets and been gentler with her, which makes it much worse.

### What she wants and fears

Brigid wants to be a healer as good as Elspeth, though she would never say so, and has no idea Elspeth thinks she will be better. She wants the old beds to come back. She fears that Elspeth will think she has failed her, and she fears, more quietly, the stretches of wild coast she now walks alone, where the forest comes right down to the rocks.

### Hooks

A quest might walk the far rocks with Brigid at low tide to guard her while she gathers, or find out what is killing the old beds. Another might help her find the words, and the courage, to tell Elspeth.
